title: Pauri 4, sound: saachaa saahib
hook: saachaa saahib saach naae bhaakhiaa bhaau apaar

segments.voice: Yesterday, veparvaahu, the carefree Giver. Your line was the giver never tires.

Back in camp three came an alarm set five minutes early for the amrit vela, the nectar hour before dawn. That hour came from somewhere specific: this pauri, the fourth step of Japji. Before the early hours, though, hear how it begins. Its first line has a sound you already know: sach, the true, from aad sach, turns up twice, in two different forms, like one word trying on two coats.
screen: `THE ALARM FIVE MINUTES EARLY.` → `IT CAME FROM THIS PAURI.` → `ONE WORD IN TWO COATS.`

segments.voice: The opening line: saachaa saahib, saach naae, bhaakhiaa bhaau apaar. Saachaa: SAA-chaa, the true one. Saahib: SAA-hib, Master, Lord; the same sahib you hear in Japji Sahib and Guru Granth Sahib, a word of honor. Saach: the true again, this time about a name. Naae: NAA-ay, name. Bhaakhiaa: BHAA-khi-aa, spoken, expressed. Bhaau: rhymes with how, with a breath on the b; it means love. Apaar: a-PAAR, without limit, boundless. So the outline is already there: true Master, true name, spoken with boundless love. Now the sound. Saachaa, saahib, saach: the line opens with three s-sounds in a row, soft and steady, like someone walking up to a door. Then bhaakhiaa bhaau, two bh sounds side by side, and the wide, open vowel of apaar. From a narrow door into a very big room. Soon the pauri turns to questions: what can we offer, what words can we say? Then a line you've heard before: amrit vela sach naau vadiaaee veechaar, the early hours, the true name, reflecting on its greatness. Then a word that opens tomorrow: nadar. For now, this first line is almost a whole prayer in miniature: who the One is, what the Name is, and how it's spoken, with love and no limit.
screen: `SAACHAA SAAHIB — TRUE MASTER.` · `SAACH NAAE — TRUE NAME.` · `BHAAU APAAR — BOUNDLESS LOVE.` · `THE AMRIT VELA LINE.` · then, large: `PAURI FOUR.`

segments.voice: Speak the first line softly: saachaa saahib, saach naae, bhaakhiaa bhaau apaar. Twice more, slower, the s-sounds soft and the last word open wide, then almost whispered. Then sit, notice how your breath lengthened on apaar, and let it stay long; if you pray, you can rest in Waheguru.
screen: `ਸਾਚਾ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਸਾਚੁ ਨਾਇ ਭਾਖਿਆ ਭਾਉ ਅਪਾਰੁ ॥`

segments.voice: Apaar. Boundless, without limit: how this pauri says love is spoken, saachaa saahib, true Master, true name.
Your line: saachaa saahib. The nectar hour before dawn starts in this pauri. Day one hundred sixty-nine, done.

howItsDone: The fourth pauri of Japji is recited each morning; its line on the amrit vela is the scriptural root of the Sikh practice of rising before dawn for simran.

original.say: SAA-chaa SAA-hib, SAACH NAA-ay, BHAA-khi-aa BHAU a-PAAR
original.note: Gurmukhi: the opening line of Japji's fourth pauri, Ang 2.

trapdoor: what you thought: true Lord, true name.
what it means: true Master, true name, spoken with boundless love: the line that leads to the amrit vela.
what a scholar hears: saahib comes into Punjabi from Arabic; bhaakhiaa, spoken, is kin to the Sanskrit bhasha, speech: both worlds in one line.
recall: the true that lasts, a name for the One
to recite and remember, again and again
